title: Per-group metrics: ingest rate, lag, storage
description:
Break down the existing aggregate Prometheus metrics by newsgroup so operators can identify hot groups, lagging peers, and storage outliers.

Why this issue exists:
Current /metrics output is aggregate across all groups. An operator cannot tell from metrics alone that comp.lang.rust has 0 articles while alt.test is receiving 1000/sec, or that one group's log is 3 reconcile cycles behind a peer. Per-group metrics are the first thing operators ask for when debugging peering or storage issues.

Scope:
New or extended Prometheus metrics, all labeled with group=<newsgroup>:
- articles_ingested_total{group} — counter, articles accepted and written to IPFS
- articles_rejected_total{group, reason} — counter, articles rejected (duplicate, invalid, backpressure)
- group_log_entries_total{group} — gauge, current log length
- group_log_lag{group, peer} — gauge, entries behind each connected peer (0 = fully reconciled)
- group_storage_bytes{group} — gauge, estimated bytes pinned for this group (sampled, not exact)
- group_last_activity_timestamp{group} — gauge, Unix timestamp of last article ingested

High-cardinality guard: if more than 500 groups are active, per-group metrics are disabled and a warning is emitted. Aggregate metrics continue regardless.

Acceptance criteria:
- /metrics includes articles_ingested_total with a group label for each subscribed group
- group_log_lag is 0 for all groups when two peered transit nodes are fully reconciled
- Grafana dashboard sample (JSON) in docs/ops/ showing per-group ingest rate and lag panels
- High-cardinality guard fires and logs a warning when more than 500 groups are subscribed
